elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance on expiry or termination for up to 6 months
elements.evidence: "at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to 6 months"

elements.element: Transition assistance priced at then-current rates
Return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format

"within 30 days after such expiry or termination"

elements.element: Deletion after return and certification of deletion
elements.evidence: "thereafter delete such Client Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing"
"transition assistance for up to 6 months" (exceeds 90 days)
"in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after such expiry or termination"

reasons: The inserted Section 14a supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: up to 6 months' assistance, then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days of expiry or termination, and post-return deletion with written certification.

The "at Client's request" qualifier attaches only to transition assistance (a natural request-driven service) and does not condition the mandatory data return, deletion, or certification in (b) and (c).

Contrary to the deterministic check flagging the 30-day trigger, the operative text expressly states "within 30 days after such expiry or termination", so the trigger and period are complete on the face of the clause.
Minimality holds: the Agreement had no exit mechanics at all, and the drafter added a single concise clause without rewriting Sections 13 or 14 or importing fallback-only language.

Intent is preserved: term, non-renewal notice, name-server/hosting migration duties and Client's domain ownership remain untouched, and the clause uses existing defined terms (Client, TrueLink, Client Content) with no dangling mechanic.
